results.name: edit the existing default header of every corpus document that has one: python-docx sees the new text with live PAGE/NUMPAGES fields; every other paragraph, part and the body are unchanged
add a header AND a footer to every corpus document that has none: new parts, relationships, content types and section references that python-docx resolves
different first page: a first-page header is created, <w:titlePg/> is set in schema order, the default header stays; switching it off keeps both parts
untouched header paragraphs keep their exact XML; locked lines (pictures, DATE/STYLEREF/… fields, links) survive an edit of the same header byte-for-byte
remove: the section no longer references the header (python-docx: linked to previous), body and footer unchanged; no-edit save stays byte-identical

hostile input: over-long text and too many lines are capped, XML specials escaped, invalid XML characters dropped, tabs become <w:tab/>, braces other than the two fields stay text — and every result opens in python-docx
lines holding other fields (DATE complex field, STYLEREF fldSimple) or a hyperlink are locked: sent back with changed text they stay byte-identical and python-docx still sees the fields

undo (Writer's snapshot/restore replayed): add → undo, remove → undo, first-page → undo each save a valid package with exactly one <w:sectPr> and the ORIGINAL references; page setup after a header edit keeps both
three-column headers (positional tabs): an edited line keeps its centre/right <w:ptab/> elements, so python-docx and our reader see the same three columns
